THE MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT; AND MINISTER OF

(a) to (e): For the first time, the definition of ‘gig workers’ and ‘platform workers’

pages.original_text:
20.07.2026 84
to finance these welfare schemes for which one of the sources is contribution
from aggregators who have to give between 1 to 2% of their annual turnover
subject to the limit of 5% of the amount paid or payable by an aggregator to
such workers. The Code has provided for constitution of National Social
Security Board with representatives from aggregators, gig and platform
workers, expert members and State Governments. Under the Code, the Board
is mandated to recommend the Central Government for framing suitable
schemes for gig workers and platform workers, monitor such social welfare
schemes for gig workers and platform workers as are administered by the
Central Government, review the expenditure from the fund and designated
bank account maintained thereunder for social security and welfare of gig and
platform workers and undertake such other functions as are assigned to it by
the Central Government from time to time.
Further, the Social Security (Central) Rules, 2026, notified on
08.05.2026, mark a significant step towards extending formal social protection
to gig and platform workers. The Rules operationalize the provisions of the
Code by mandating registration of gig and platform workers on the Central
Government portal, requiring aggregators to share worker-related data
through Application Programming Interface (API) or other electronic means,
prescribing eligibility criteria for social security benefits, and strengthening
accountability of aggregators in relation to welfare measures for such workers.

20.07.2026 85
The Government in its Budget announcement for financial year 2025-26
had announced several key measures for the welfare of Gig workers of online
platforms (platform workers) viz. their registration on the eShram portal,
issuance of identity cards, and extension of health care benefits under
Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY).
The Ministry of Labour and Employment had launched eShram portal on
26.08.2021 for creation of a comprehensive National Database of Unorganised
Workers including platform workers, migrant workers etc. The eShram portal is
meant to register and support the unorganised workers by providing them a
Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis. The Ministry of
Labour and Employment has also launched the eShram- ‘One-Stop-Solution’
that entails integration of different social security/welfare schemes at single
portal i.e., eShram portal. This is envisaged to enable unorganised workers
including platform workers registered on eShram to access social security
schemes including health care benefits under AB-PMJAY and see benefits
availed by them so far, through eShram portal.
The Ministry has also launched a dedicated Aggregator Module on
12.12.2024 for onboarding of aggregators on eShram portal. Till date, 21
aggregators including Zomato, Blinkit, Swiggy, Ola, Uber, Rapido, Amazon,
Porter, Urban Company, Flipkart etc. have onboarded on eShram portal. Also,
Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) have been developed on this
Module for verification and sharing details of platform workers engaged with
the aggregators.

20.07.2026 86
A simplified Registration Module for platform workers has been launched
on 12.03.2025 on the eShram portal to facilitate platform workers to register
themselves or update their occupation, if already registered on eShram portal.
To maximise registration of platform workers on eShram portal, three
nationwide special registration drives were held during the months of April,
May and August-September, 2025 in collaboration with States and Union
Territories. As on 14.07.2026, over 10.65 lakh platform workers are registered
on eShram portal.
The Ministry of Labour & Employment has conducted multiple rounds of
deliberations with Aggregators, Knowledge Partners, Platform Workers
Associations, State Government/Union Territories and other organisations for
social security framework of gig and platform workers to move forward for a
comprehensive welfare scheme for platform workers across the country, as
mandated under the Code.

*9. ADV. GOWAAL KAGADA PADAVI:
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of schemes
such as Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and Skill India
Digital Hub (SIDH) in tribal and aspirational districts, particularly in
Maharashtra including Nandurbar district;
(b) whether limited vocational training institutes, poor digital infrastructure,
weak industry-linked programmes and low placement rates continue to
affect skill development outcomes in remote tribal regions and if so, the
details thereof;
(c) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under the said
schemes during the last three years and the current year in the said State
and districts;
(d) whether delays in implementation, accessibility barriers and low
participation of women and tribal youth have been reported under the said
schemes and if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the corrective measures taken/being taken by the Government to improve
placement- linked skill development and digital training access in tribal
districts like Nandurbar?

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a) and (b): Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has
been implementing its flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana
(PMKVY), since 2015, for imparting skill development training through Short-
Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of Prior
Learning (RPL), to all sections of the society across the country, including in
tribal and aspirational districts. The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) serves as an
integrated digital platform providing access to skill courses, career guidance,
apprenticeship opportunities and other skilling-related services. These
initiatives are implemented across all States/UTs, including Maharashtra and
its tribal districts such as Nandurbar.
PMKVY 4.0 is a demand driven Scheme and skill training centres are
accredited and affiliated based on the requirements received from State/
industry/ industry associations/ training providers.
MSDE conducts periodic independent evaluations of PMKVY to ensure
quality and accountability. An evaluation by NITI Aayog (October 2020)
indicated that approximately 94 percent of surveyed employers expressed
willingness to hire more candidates trained under PMKVY. The study also
noted that 52 percent of candidates placed in employment or oriented under
the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) component reported receiving higher
salaries or expecting improved earnings compared to uncertified peers. An

Learning (RPL), to all sections of the society across the country, including in
tribal and aspirational districts. The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) serves as an
integrated digital platform providing access to skill courses, career guidance,
apprenticeship opportunities and other skilling-related services. These
initiatives are implemented across all States/UTs, including Maharashtra and
its tribal districts such as Nandurbar.
PMKVY 4.0 is a demand driven Scheme and skill training centres are
accredited and affiliated based on the requirements received from State/
industry/ industry associations/ training providers.
MSDE conducts periodic independent evaluations of PMKVY to ensure
quality and accountability. An evaluation by NITI Aayog (October 2020)
indicated that approximately 94 percent of surveyed employers expressed
willingness to hire more candidates trained under PMKVY. The study also
noted that 52 percent of candidates placed in employment or oriented under
the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) component reported receiving higher
salaries or expecting improved earnings compared to uncertified peers. An

independent evaluation of PMKVY 2.0 conducted by the Indian Institute of

candidates were placed in their desired skill sector.
More recently, an independent third-party impact evaluation of the
PMKVY 4.0 has been conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial
Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous institution of Ministry of Finance,
Government of India, across the country including the State of Maharashtra.
The Study also covered aspirational and tribal districts. As per the report,
PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in employment
outcomes for STT candidates. The combined share of employed and self-
employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4%
after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income-
related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates
and 48.9% of RPL candidates reporting an increase in income following
training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded
access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable
improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income
outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries.

Forest Survey of India (FSI) under Ministry of Environment, Forest &
Climate Change carries out the assessment of forest and tree cover of the
country biennially and the findings are published in the India State of Forest
Report (ISFR). The forest cover assessment is a wall-to-wall mapping exercise
based on remote sensing supported by intensive ground verification and field
data from the National Forest Inventory. ISFR 2023 provides State/UT-wise
information on forest cover, tree cover, mangrove cover, growing stock, carbon
stock, forest fire monitoring and changes in forest cover, which constitute
important indicators for assessing the ecological status of forests.

identifying areas requiring conservation, restoration and sustainable forest
management interventions. The State/UT-wise assessment of forest and tree
cover is given in the enclosed Statement-II.

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE; AND MINISTER OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS
(SHRIMATI NIRMALA SITHARAMAN):
(a): The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) consolidates the laws
relating to reorganisation and insolvency resolution of corporate persons,
partnership firms and individuals in a time bound manner for maximisation of
value of assets of such persons. The IBC has established four pillars of
insolvency namely the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India, defined the
Adjudicating Authority, Information Utility and the Insolvency Professionals.
(b): In the pre-IBC period, there was no single law that dealt with insolvency
and bankruptcy. The Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985,
the Recovery of Debt Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993, the
Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of
Security Interest Act, 2002 and the Companies Act, 2013 had provisions
relating to insolvency and bankruptcy. The IBC has consolidated all these
fragmented laws and resolved 1419 companies as on 31st March 2026. These
cases have led to a recovery of ₹ 4.32 lakh crore to the creditors, which
amounts to a realisation of 94.6% of fair value and 166.9% of liquidation value.
IBC has enhanced the ease of doing business by providing a time-bound and
transparent mechanism for resolving insolvency, improving investor
confidence and credit availability.

fragmented laws and resolved 1419 companies as on 31st March 2026. These
cases have led to a recovery of ₹ 4.32 lakh crore to the creditors, which
amounts to a realisation of 94.6% of fair value and 166.9% of liquidation value.
IBC has enhanced the ease of doing business by providing a time-bound and
transparent mechanism for resolving insolvency, improving investor
confidence and credit availability.

pleased to state:
(a) whether any Central financial assistance has been extended to Telangana
for human-animal conflicts mitigation during the last three years and the
current year, if so, the details thereof, year-wise and if not, the reasons
therefor;

incidents in Telangana, if so, the details thereof, district-wise and if not, the

to support Telangana in conflict mitigation, if so, the details thereof,

victims of wildlife attacks in Telangana, if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons for leaving burden entirely on the State Government; and

(e) whether the Government has any data of the total compensation disbursed
in Telangana for human deaths, injuries, livestock loss and crop damage, if
so, the details thereof, category-wise and if not, the reasons for lack of
consolidated data?
THE MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE
(SHRI BHUPENDER YADAV):
(a): The management of wildlife including mitigation of human-animal
conflicts is primarily the responsibility of the concerned State
Government/Union Territory Administration. The State Government/UT
Administration are the first responders to any conflict situation and they
maintain the details of the conflict along with the species involved. Under the
Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats
an amount of Rs. 323.32 lakhs, Rs. 291.68 lakhs, Rs. 302.34 lakhs and Rs.
208.67 lakhs have been released to the State of Telangana during the
financial years 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 & 2026-27 respectively for inter
alia management of Human wildlife conflict.
(b) to (e): Under the said scheme, activities supported include procurement
of early warning systems, construction and erection of physical barriers such
as solar powered electric fencing, bio-fencing, trenches, boundary walls etc.
to prevent depredation by wild animals which inter alia includes cattle lifting,
crop damage, loss of life and property. Rapid Response Teams with
community stewards are also deployed to mitigate Human-Wildlife Conflict.

in respect of compensation and affected districts is collated at level of the
State.
Important steps taken by the Government to manage human-wildlife
conflicts include the following:

incentives. The scheme provides for incentives for 1.92 crore eligible First

outreach effort, PM-VBRY events were also organised simultaneously at
around 200 locations across the country.

establishments.

collaboration between academia, industry and international institutions.

in the Global Innovation Index (GII) from 48 in 2020 and currently being ranked
at 38th place in 2025.

enabled the setting up of Foreign Higher Educational Institutions (FHEIs) in
India. 16 Letters of Intent have been issued to FHEIs from Australia, Italy,
United Kingdom and USA to set up their campuses at various places in India.
Among these, University of Southampton, UK commenced its courses in
August, 2025 at its campus in Gurugram, Haryana. Under International
Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) Regulations 2022, approvals
have been accorded to 5 universities from UK, Australia and Northern Ireland
for operating offshore branch campuses in GIFT City SEZ, Gandhinagar,
Gujarat. Among these 5 universities, Deakin University, Australia commenced
its courses in July, 2024, and University of Wollongong, Australia commenced
its courses in November, 2024. In addition, Indian institutions are also
establishing a global presence, with IIT Delhi’s campus in Abu Dhabi, IIM
Ahmedabad campus in Dubai and IIT Madras in Tanzania. These steps
support the goal of making India a global hub for education.

Administration (NIEPA). This initiative aims to strengthen the wardens’ capacity

administrative skills, thereby fostering a safe and supportive environment that
promotes and improves quality education for girls.

THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI

and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive” (PRASHAD) provides financial
assistance to the State Governments (SGs) and Union Territory
Administrations (UTAs) for development of tourism related infrastructure at
identified religious and heritage sites across the country including the State of
Tamil Nadu. The details of the total funds sanctioned, released and utilized
under the said scheme, State/UT wise including Tamil Nadu are given in the
enclosed Statement.

experience and the overall development of pilgrimage destinations.

(c) and (d): The Labour Codes were enacted to meet need for comprehensive
labour reforms that formalize employment, simplify compliance through digital
integration, strengthen social Security and ensure workplace safety and
equality. The Codes will provide universal minimum wages and social security
benefits for workers.
The gig workers and the platform workers have been defined for the first
time in the Labour Code for the purpose of formulating schemes to provide
social security benefits relating to life and disability cover, accident insurance,
health and maternity benefits, old age protection etc.
The Labour Codes have several enabling provisions which will promote
formalisation and employment generation including social security and welfare
of the workers. Such provisions include, formalization of employment through
mandatory issue of appointment letter, universalisation of social security by
extending coverage to organised, unorganised, gig and platform workers to
strengthen their protection against employment-related vulnerabilities and
enabling greater adaptability to new forms of work like gig & platform work and
technology-driven employment models.

Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:

and Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) sector to improve transparency,
accountability and operational efficiency, if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor;
(b) whether the Government is considering granting banking licenses to eligible

thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;

performance of Regional Rural Banks particularly in Madhya Pradesh and
Maharashtra, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) whether measures have been taken to improve governance and strategic
oversight of public financial institutions, if so, the details thereof; and

(e) the expected impact of these reforms on strengthening the banking sector
and expanding institutional credit access?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PANKAJ
CHOUDHARY):
(a): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has apprised that strengthening of corporate
governance frameworks in banks is an ongoing exercise undertaken by RBI to
ensure a robust, transparent and efficient banking system aligned with global best
practices.
In the recent past, RBI has issued instructions pertaining to independence
of Board and Board Committees, quorum requirements, requirement for a bank
Chairperson to be an Independent Director, age and tenure limits, fit and proper
criteria, succession planning, remuneration etc., in respect of Non-executive
Directors (NEDs) as well as Whole-time Directors (WTDs), etc.
(b): In terms of the guidelines issued by RBI on ‘On-tap’ licensing of Universal
Banks and Small Finance Banks in the Private Sector, dated 28.11.2025, existing
NBFCs are permitted to apply to the Reserve Bank for promoting or conversion to
Universal Bank and Small Finance Bank.
(c): As regards RRBs, the existing instructions on Governance, Board procedures,
Committees of the Board etc. have been consolidated and issued as ‘RBI (RRBs-
Governance) Directions’ on 28.11.2025. For better governance, Government has
appointed Government Nominee Directors in the board of all RRBs. Further,

oversight on their governance and operational matters.

functioning of PFIs and provide strategic guidance, wherever necessary.

operational efficiency, and promote sound and resilient financial institutions

More recently, an independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY
4.0 has been conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial
Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous institution of Ministry of Finance,
Government of India, across the country including the State of Maharashtra. As
per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift in
employment outcomes for STT candidates. The combined share of employed and
self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4%
after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8 percentage point increase. Income-
related outcomes also show positive movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates
and 48.9% of RPL candidates reporting an increase in income following training
and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to formal
skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill
confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial
proportion of beneficiaries.

Economy intervention, namely Rachnatmak Bharat, for the promotion and
development of the cultural and creative economy which envisages support for
capacity building, market access, innovation, digital enablement and institutional
strengthening to foster sustainable growth of the creative economy, including
support for emerging artists and creative practitioners.
The Ministry through its Zonal Culture Centres and Akademies provide a
platform to emerging artists by engaging them in various cultural programmes,
festivals, workshops and exhibitions organized across their member States.
These engagements enable artists to showcase their talent, gain wider exposure
and preserve and promote traditional art forms. The artists are also provided
honorarium, TA/DA, boarding and lodging, local transport etc. which help
supplement their income and encourage them to pursue their art as a sustainable
livelihood, thereby contributing to their self-reliance.

cooperative bank has been considered, if so, the present status thereof;

governance, loan portfolio, asset quality, management of the bank, if so, the

of Pollution) Act, 1974 & The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to prevent
and control pollution of aquatic resources.

direct concerned agencies in the State/UT to develop infrastructure for sewage
treatment.

specific effluent discharge standards under the Environment (Protection)
Rules, 1986 with an aim to prevent pollution in the water bodies.

schemes for which one of the sources is contribution from aggregators between 1

paid or payable by an aggregator to such workers. The Code also has provisions
to constitute a National Social Security Board for the purposes of the welfare of
gig workers and platform workers.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):
(a) and (b): The Government has notified the Hazardous and Other Wastes
(Management and Transboundary Movement) (HOWM) Rules, 2016 in
supersession of the Hazardous Wastes (Management, Handling and
Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2008 under the Environment (Protection) Act,
1986, which provide a comprehensive regulatory framework for environmentally
sound management of hazardous wastes, including Spent Pot Lining (SPL). SPL,
generated during production of primary and secondary aluminium is categorized
as a hazardous waste under Item 11.2 of Schedule-I of the HOWM Rules, 2016.
The Rules do not permit the use or sale of SPL as commercial coal or its mixing
with coal for supply to industrial units. SPL is required to be managed through
authorized recyclers, pre-processors, co-processors, actual users or Treatment,
Storage and Disposal Facilities (TSDFs), as applicable, and its movement is
regulated through the prescribed manifest system.

framework for the environmentally sound collection, transportation, refurbishment
and recycling of scrap of non-ferrous metals, namely aluminium, copper, zinc and
their alloys, covering producers, manufacturers, collection agents, refurbishers,
recyclers and bulk consumers. The Rules mandate registration of all stakeholders
on the CPCB portal, prescribe recycling targets for producers through the EPR
mechanism, require manufacturers to ensure utilisation of recycled non-ferrous
metals, provide for generation and trading of EPR certificates by registered
recyclers, and require maintenance of records and filing of returns to facilitate
digital tracking, monitoring and enforcement of compliance.

Committee. The Board of the company is required to disclose the CSR Policy

purposes and in the manner as approved by it, and the Chief Financial Officer or
the person responsible for financial management shall certify to the effect. In
case any amount remains unspent then such amount shall be transferred in the
designated fund(s) in Schedule VII in the prescribed time limit. Further, the first
proviso to Section 135 (5) of the Act provides that the company shall give
preference to the local area and areas around it where it operates. However, the
emphasis on local area is only directory and not mandatory in nature and
companies need to balance local area preference with national priorities.

formulation of CSR policy, Annual Action Plan on CSR, identification of the
project and area in which project will be implemented, certification of CSR
expenditure by Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and audit of CSR expenditure by
statutory auditors, etc., provide adequate mechanisms to ensure transparency
and accountability.
Whenever any violation of CSR provisions is reported, action against such
non-compliant Companies is initiated as per provisions of the Companies Act,
2013 and rules made thereunder after due examination of records and following
due process of law.

community benefit.

six months of training, and 60 percent of previously non-earning individuals
starting to earn post-training.

created and regularly updated and if so, the access details thereof and if not,
the reasons for absence of transparent digital tracking systems; and
(e) whether the Government has taken steps to prevent ongoing smuggling of
temple idols and artefacts and if so, the enforcement measures thereof and if
not, the reasons for continued illicit trafficking networks?

(a) and (c): Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) aims to nudge individuals and
communities to practice a lifestyle that is synchronous with nature through Whole-
of-Government and Whole-of-Society approach focusing on seven themes viz.,
Save Energy, Save Water, Reduce Waste, Reduce E-Waste, Say No to Single
Use Plastic, Adopt Healthy Lifestyles and Adopt Sustainable Food Systems. The
major activities undertaken under Mission LiFE since its launch in October, 2022
include the following:
 Nationwide mass mobilization campaigns such as “One Nation One Mission:
End Plastic Pollution”, “Harit Yoga” (on the eve of International Day of Yoga
2025), Swachhata Hi Sewa campaigns, World Environment Day pre-
campaigns, etc have been undertaken to create awareness on Mission LiFE.
The flagship “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative has resonated with one and all
and over 272 Crore saplings have been planted under the same.
 Mission LiFE principles added to India’s Nationally Determined Contributions
(NDCs) under the Paris Agreement.
 Under the Ministry’s Environment Education Programme, students actively
participate in workshops, nature camps, exhibitions, competitions, and summer
programmes promoting sustainable habits. The Environment Information,
Awareness, Capacity Building and Livelihood Programme (EIACP) Centres
under the Ministry also organize mass outreach and capacity-building activities
on various themes of Mission LiFE.

NITI Aayog has undertaken an independent third-party evaluation of
Centrally Sponsored Schemes under DoSE&L, including the STARS Project. The
evaluation findings indicate that the Project has contributed to strengthening
outcome-oriented planning, learning assessment systems and evidence-based
decision-making processes in the school education sector.
(d) and (e): This is to state that the STARS Project was approved initially for a

scheme has been further extended by two years (till 31st March 2027) at no
additional cost to support the states for completion of already approved non-
recurring activities.
The STARS Project is being implemented in six States, namely Himachal
Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Kerala and
there is no such proposal of inclusion of any other state in the scheme.

Central Government, the Central Industial Relations Machinery (CIRM) is
entrusted with the task of maintaining good industrial relations and protecting the
interest of workers including in matters relating to termination, retrenchment or
lay-off and its prevention.
The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 contains various provisions to
safeguard workers' rights and job security, including statutory safeguards in the
form of mandatory notice period, retrenchment compensation and provision for
retrenched workers to be given preference in re-employment are applicable for
all retrenched workers. The Code also introduces Workers Re-skilling fund for
training of retrenched workers for the first time with a view to providing financial
support to retrenched workers to utilize that amount for his re-skilling. The
Negotiating Unions/Negotiating Councils have been brought under the statutory
provisions to strengthen collective bargaining.

National Virtual Library of India (NVLI) presently known as India Culture
Portal (ICP):
The National Virtual Library of India (NVLI) was envisaged as a digital platform
to provide unified access to India's cultural resources through a user-friendly
multilingual interface. The Ministry of Culture entrusted its development to IIT
Bombay. The initiative has since evolved into the Indian Culture Portal, which
aggregates digital and bibliographic resources from various cultural institutions.
As a major milestone, Indian Culture Portal 2.0 was launched on 05.03.2026
with a modern React-based frontend and Drupal backend, offering improved
performance, enhanced search capabilities, and the AI-powered chatbot.

BANKING AND FINANCIAL ACCESS IN LADAKH
110. SHRI MOHMAD HANEEFA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has taken steps to increase the number of
functional bank branches, ATMs, and micro-financing institutions in remote
areas of UT Ladakh, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether any guidelines exist to incentivize banks to expand financial
services in difficult terrain and zero-network zones of Ladakh, if so, the
details thereof;
(c) whether the Government is aware of the difficulties faced by the people of
Ladakh in accessing Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT), loans, and pension
schemes due to connectivity or administrative challenges; and
(d) if so, whether the Government proposes to collaborate with India Post
Payments Bank (IPPB), Common Service Centres (CSCs) or post offices
for mobile banking and Aadhaar-based financial services in inaccessible
regions?

monitored by a Geographic Information System (GIS) based App., namely, Jan
Dhan Darshak (JDD) App.

uncovered areas is a continuous process looked after by the State Level
Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) / Union Territory Level Bankers Committee

SCHEMES TO FORTIFY THE COASTAL SHELTER IN BALASORE
112. SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be
pleased to state?
(a) whether the Government has details about the schemes/programmes
implemented in Balasore district of Odisha to deal with the constant
flooding to ensure fortification of the coastal shelter belt;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) the details of funds apportioned and expended for this endeavour during
the last five years;
(d) the details of accomplishments attained hitherto in terms of the area
encompassed under mangrove and casuarina plantations in the said
district;
(e) whether the Government has faced impediments in effectuating this project
in the said district; and
(f) if so, the steps taken by the Government to surmount these impediments
and ensure the punctual completion of this project?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):

(a) and (b): Coastal Protection Works are undertaken by the respective State
Governments/UTs. Various state and central sponsored programs are being
implemented to enhance coastal resilience in Balasore district, which inter-alia
includes:
(i) Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI) - A
central scheme dedicated to the intensive restoration and plantation of
mangroves along the coastline to mitigate storm surges and flooding.
(ii) State Plan/Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning
Authority (CAMPA) - State funded compensatory afforestation and resource
management programs are used to erect natural barriers against cyclone winds,
coastal erosion and tidal ingress by Casuarina plantations.
(iii) Enhancing Climate Resilience of India's Coastal Communities (ECRICC): A
climate adaptation project by the Green Climate Fund to tackle the twin issues
of sustainable development and climate resilience in coastal areas.

(e) and (f): As per the State Forest Department, Odisha, the key impediments
faced in the mangrove and casuarina plantation include hydrological alterations,
predation and pests, monospecific plantations, soil degradation, displacement of
native flora and limited storm-buffer efficacy.
The steps taken to overcome such impediments for mangrove plantation
include restoration of hydrology to create favourable conditions for seedling
establishment and long term survival; use of native, site-specific species to
enhance biodiversity and ecological resilience; protection from grazing and
pests through fencing, community surveillance and periodic monitoring; planting
of healthy, disease free seedlings; regular monitoring and timely replanting
during suitable planting seasons.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a) and (b): The Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the aegis of

pages.original_text:

respective State Governments. However, DGT has supported the upgradation of
ITIs as per the needs highlighted by State/UT Governments through various
schemes, such as the Upgradation of Existing Government ITIs into Model ITIs
and the Skill Strengthening for Industrial Value Enhancement (STRIVE)
Scheme. A Tracer Study to assess employment outcomes of ITI pass outs from
Skills Strengthening for Industrial Value Enhancement (STRIVE) Scheme was
conducted in 2024, wherein one of the parameter for the study was
modernisation of infrastructure of ITIs. Further, as per the study report 78.8
percent of the respondents expressed satisfaction with the infrastructure at ITI.
(c): Under STRIVE, a total financial assistance of Rs. 25.88 crore was provided
to the State of Andhra Pradesh for the upgradation of 15 ITIs. Additionally, the
State-wise details of fund release under the Upgradation of Existing
Government ITIs into Model ITIs scheme are given in the enclosed Statement-I.
(d) and (e): Upgradation of curricula for ITI training programmes is a continuous
process and is generally undertaken every three years. During the last five
years, 21 Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) courses, 15 short-term courses 17
Flexi-MoU courses and one Craft Instructor Training Scheme (CITS) have been
developed and approved by National Council for Vocational Education and
Training (NCVET). Additionally, 40 CTS courses have been revised and
approved to further align training with industry requirements. The list is attached
at enclosed Statement-II.

Initiatives for enhancing employability, workforce readiness,
apprenticeship opportunities and skill upgradation: In order to meet
skilling requirement for future workforce, improve the quality of skilling, to align
the training programs to market needs and improve the employability of
trainees, some of the steps taken by the Government include:
i. The training programs offered under the schemes of the Ministry are
developed in collaboration with industries, keeping in view the market
demands.
ii. Courses aligned to National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) also
have components of On Job Training (OJT) and employability skills.
iii. The National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET)
has been set up as an overarching regulator establishing regulations
and standards to ensure quality in the Technical and Vocational
Education and Training (TVET) space. The Awarding Bodies
recognized by NCVET are required to develop the qualifications as per
the industry demand and obtain industry validations.
iv. Future ready job-roles addressing the requirement of Industry 4.0,
emerging sectors like Drone, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics,
Mechatronics, etc., have been prioritized under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal
Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0.

(a) the details of total number of artists, artisans and cultural practitioners
registered under the National Mission on Cultural Mapping (NMCM),
State/UT-wise;
(b) the details of number of cultural clusters identified and documented under
the said Mission;
(c) whether any financial assistance, insurance or social security support has
been extended to registered artists under the said Mission, and if so, the
details thereof; and
(d) the details of steps taken by the Government to integrate the Cultural
Mapping database with tourism, education and skill development
initiatives?
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI
GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):
(a): The National Mission on Cultural Mapping (NMCM), through the Mera
Gaon Meri Dharohar (MGMD) initiative, undertakes village-level cultural
mapping across the country. Cultural information relating to artists, artisans and
other cultural practitioners, wherever available, is documented as part of village

cultural profiles. However, NMCM does not provide for registration of artists or
cultural practitioners. The data on the MGMD Portal is maintained village-wise

artisans and cultural practitioners is not maintained. An illustrative list of artists,
artisans and cultural practitioners documented under MGMD is given in the

cultural information in village profiles. Separate data on cultural clusters is not
maintained under the Mission. However, an illustrative list of cultural institutions

Statement-II.
(c): NMCM undertakes documentation of cultural assets, including artists and
cultural practitioners. The Mission does not provide for registration of artists.

provided under NMCM.

heritage. At present, there is no provision under the Mission for integration of
the cultural mapping database with tourism, education or skill development
initiatives.

NATIONAL AUDIT ON GOVERNMENT SCHOOLS
132. SHRI RAMASAHAYAM RAGHURAM REDDY:
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether any national audit has been conducted recently on the quality of
teaching and infrastructure in Government schools;
(b) if so, the proportion of schools without functional toilets, internet access,
or science labs, State/UT-wise;
(c) whether the Government is considering a minimum per-student
infrastructure budget if so, the details thereof States/UT-wise;
(d) whether implementation of National Education Policy (NEP) has resulted
in improved student learning outcomes; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a): The quality of school education and infrastructure is monitored, audited
and assessed through various institutional mechanisms, including the
Performance Grading Index (PGI), UDISE+, PARAKH assessments, PM SHRI
School Quality Monitoring Framework, social audit and periodic review and
monitoring under the Samagra Shiksha Scheme. Further, States/UTs
undertake monitoring and evaluation of schools as per their respective
administrative arrangements.

reflecting the positive impact of the NIPUN Bharat Mission launched under
NEP 2020. Further, Central Government schools demonstrate the strongest
performance in all subjects at the preparatory and middle stage, suggesting
returns from improved infrastructure and increased per child spending in such
schools.

(a): National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched in August
2016. The scheme was extended to continue as NAPS-2 from FY 2022-23.
Under, NAPS 2.0, the stipend support by Government of India (GoI) is paid
through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the bank account of apprentices. The
number of apprentices engaged in the State of Andhra Pradesh from FY 2022-23
till FY 2026-27 (upto 30.06.2026) is 93,094. The details of district-wise and year-
wise apprentices engaged in the State of Andhra Pradesh are given in the
enclosed Statement-I.

conducted within an establishment/industry. The number of establishment/
industries in Andhra Pradesh which have engaged apprentices under NAPS 2.0
(FY 2022-23 till FY 2026-27 (upto 30.06.2026)) are 1,135 unique establishments.

which have engaged apprentices in the State of Andhra Pradesh are given in the
enclosed Statement-II and III.

INTERVENTIONS OF SAMAGRA SHIKSHA SCHEME IN MADHYA PRADESH
135. SHRI VISHNU DATT SHARMA:
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Samagra Shiksha (Integrated School Education) scheme
interventions (infrastructure, digital education, vocational integration and
teacher training) are being implemented in Katni, Panna and Khajuraho
town in Madhya Pradesh, if so, the details thereof;

pages.original_text:
20.07.2026 881
(b) the specific infrastructure, digital/ICT and teacher-training works sanctioned
and completed in schools of these districts during the last three years;
(c) the number of schools covered, funds released and measurable outcomes
achieved in the said districts;
(d) whether coverage of the said scheme is inadequate in the said districts, if so,
the reasons therefor; and
(e) the details of timeframe and planned interventions to ensure equitable
school-education quality and employability-linked vocational programmes in
these districts?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a): Scheme of Samagra Shiksha supports State/UTs for various infrastructure
interventions like opening /strengthening of Schools, upgradation of schools,
additional classrooms, toilets, drinking water, electrification, different labs, various
residential facilities including KGBVs, NSCBAVs, PM JANMAN and DAJGUA etc.
To promote Digital Education, ICT/Smart classes, internet connectivity, digital
library are also supported. Under Skill/Vocational Education intervention, financial
assistance is provided to States/UTs for giving exposure to Skill Education to
students of Grades 6 to 8 and introduction of Skill courses from Grades 9 to 12,
which are aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT

(a): Scheme of Samagra Shiksha supports State/UTs for various infrastructure
interventions like opening /strengthening of Schools, upgradation of schools,
additional classrooms, toilets, drinking water, electrification, different labs, various
residential facilities including KGBVs, NSCBAVs, PM JANMAN and DAJGUA etc.
To promote Digital Education, ICT/Smart classes, internet connectivity, digital
library are also supported. Under Skill/Vocational Education intervention, financial
assistance is provided to States/UTs for giving exposure to Skill Education to
students of Grades 6 to 8 and introduction of Skill courses from Grades 9 to 12,
which are aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF).

pages.original_text:
20.07.2026 882
These Samagra Shiksha interventions are being implemented throughout the
country including all districts of Madhya Pradesh.
(b) to (d): All the States/UTs prepare annual plans as per their
requirement/priority, and the same is reflected in their respective Annual Work
Plan and Budget (AWP&B) proposals, as per norms of Samagra Shiksha scheme.
These plans are then appraised and approved by the Project Approval Board
(PAB) in the Department of School Education & Literacy in consultation with the
States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme and
physical and financial progress of the States/UTs for the interventions approved
earlier. As informed by the State Government of Madhya Pradesh, the details on
infrastructure, digital/ICT and teacher-training works sanctioned and completed in
schools of districts Katni, Panna and Chhatarpur (Khajuraho) during the last three
years are given in the enclosed Statement.
Further, Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the
Nation’s One Nation, One Digital platform for providing quality e-content for
school education in States/UTs including the above mentioned districts. As a
participant in DIKSHA, States/UTs/Autonomous Bodies have generated content in
mother local/regional languages enabling multilingualism. The platform supports
both online and offline access, enabling learners to download content and
continue learning without internet connectivity.

(d) whether any measures have been taken by the Government to disburse

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI PANKAJ
CHOUDHARY):
(a) and (b): Since 2024, 11 individuals have been declared as Fugitive
Economic Offenders under the provisions of the Fugitive Economic Offenders
Act, 2018 (FEOA). Properties amounting to ₹ 1,303.16 crore have been
confiscated under the provisions of Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018
pertaining to such offenders since 2024.
(c): Out of the above said fugitives, Red Notice has been published against 08
individuals and Extradition Requests have been sent in respect of 04
individuals who were located. Moreover, 12 Mutual Legal Assistance Requests
(MLAR) have also been sent.
(d): Yes, necessary steps have been taken by the Government to restitute the
confiscated property to the legitimate victims of such economic offences. So
far, the Directorate has successfully restored properties valued at
approximately ₹ 73,015.03 crore to victims or legitimate claimants resulting in
restitution of ₹ 15,262.30 crore and ₹ 32,677.97 crore during FY 2024-25 and
2025-26 respectively. Moreover, during the FY 2026-27 till date, an amount of
₹ 9,873.11 crore has been restituted.

To support skill development, the SWAYAM Plus portal has also been
launched, focusing on upskilling and reskilling the workforce. More than 500
courses have been developed curated from 89 industry partners across 17
sectors and offered on emerging areas such as AI, Data Analyst etc. So far,
more than 6,00,000 students registered on the platform.
The National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS) bridges the gap
between academic learning and industry requirements by providing structured
on-the-job training to graduates and diploma holders. The Scheme promotes
industry-integrated education through Apprenticeship Embedded Degree
Programmes (AEDP), supports apprenticeships in emerging areas such as
Artificial Intelligence (AI), and facilitates academic credit integration through the
NATS Assessment and Creditisation Framework. During the last five financial
years, over 12.94 lakh apprentices have been engaged under the Scheme.
The NATS 2.0 Portal, launched on 30.07.2024, has further strengthened the
apprenticeship ecosystem by enabling participation of over 11,355 Higher
Education Institutions and more than 15,840 establishments.

(d): The Government of India has issued detailed guidelines on quality, safety
and hygiene to ensure serving of good quality nutritious meal under the
Scheme. These guidelines are available on official website
https://pmposhan.education.gov.in . These guidelines, inter-alia, provides for
instructions to schools to procure Agmark quality and branded items for
preparation of meals, training to Cook-cum-Helpers, tasting of meals by
members of School Management Committee including at least one teacher
before serving the hot meal to children. The Guidelines also provides for
training of Cook-cum-Helpers on nutrition, cooking processes, health and
hygiene, preparation of raw grains and vegetables, recipes, serving skills etc.
States/UTs are providing training to CCHs in collaboration with Ministry of
Tourism, Government of India through their Institutes of Hotel Management
and Food Craft Institutes, FSSAI, State Agricultural Universities etc. Further,
the guidelines provide for testing of food samples by Government Food
Research Laboratory or any laboratory accredited or recognized by law to
ensure that the meals meet nutritional standards and quality.

procedures, benefit-sharing mechanisms and transparency under the ABS
framework are dealt with by the respective State Biodiversity Boards/ Union
Territory Biodiversity Councils.
The non-monetary benefits provided to communities including farmers in
the States/ UTs including Andhra Pradesh, as prescribed under the Biological
Diversity (Access to Biological Resources and Knowledge Associated thereto and
Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits) Regulations, 2025 inter alia include:
i. Providing institutional capacity building;
ii. Remediation and restoration activities to prevent habitat destruction or
pollution or contamination of areas;
iii. Contribution/collaboration related to education and training in India on
conservation and sustainable use of biological resources;
iv. Setting up of production, research, and development units/facilities
contributing to the local economy and income generation for the local
communities;
v. Taking appropriate measures for conservation and protection of species
including rare, endangered and threatened species by raising nurseries
and/or plantations in the area from where biological resources have been
accessed;

(a) to (d): Rule 1 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 provides that the
GFR, 2017 shall apply to all Central Government Ministries/Departments and their
attached and subordinate bodies. Accordingly, the OM dated 02.02.2022,
whereby Rules 170(i) and 171(i) of the GFR, 2017 were amended to include
Insurance Surety Bonds (ISBs) as one of the acceptable forms of Bid Security
and Performance Security, is applicable only to the entities covered under the
GFR, 2017 and is therefore not applicable to State Governments.
However, a letter dated 08.05.2026 has been sent to Chief Secretaries of
all States to promote adoption of ISBs.

TIGER AND ELEPHANT POPULATION
156. SHRIMATI JUNE MALIAH:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleas
ed to state:
(a) the latest population of tigers and elephants in the country;
(b) whether there has been any increase or decline in their population during the
last three years;
(c) the number of deaths of tigers and elephants due to poaching, train accidents
and electrocution during the said period; and
(d) the measures taken by the Government to prevent such death?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):
(a) and (b): The tiger population has increased as per the All India Tiger
Estimation done in 2022, with an estimated number of 3682 (range 3167-3925) as
compared to the 2018 estimation of 2967 (range 2603-3346) and the details are
given in the enclosed Statement-I.
The State-wise details of wild elephants in the country, as per the latest
“Status of Elephants in India: DNA-Based Synchronous All India Population
Estimation (SAIEE) 2022-25” are given in the enclosed Statement-II. This
nationwide estimate uses DNA-based mark–recapture for the first time in India.

national importance, including Indian Institutes of Management (IIM), across
India, after taking into account regional balance and resource availability.

Goa, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim do not have an
IIM.

implementation of universal social security for unorganised workers?

Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) seeded with Aadhaar. eShram portal

SYM), National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), etc. The eShram
database enables targeted identification and inclusion of eligible beneficiaries,
promotes portability of benefits for migrant workers and supports evidence-based
policy formulation, thereby expanding social security coverage and improving
access to benefits for unorganised workers across the country.

177. SHRI BENNY BEHANAN:
SHRI K. RADHAKRISHNAN:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that unemployment rate among youth aged 15-29 years
has risen in the last two years as per Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)
data;
(b) if so, the details thereof, year and State-wise;
(c) the reasons for job losses in Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
and manufacturing sectors despite ‘Make in India’ claims; and

pages.original_text:

the time by which results are expected?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF MICRO, SMALL AND
MEDIUM ENTERPRISES; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (KUMARI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE):
(a) to (d): The official data on Employment and Unemployment is collected
through Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), which is conducted by Ministry of
Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) since 2017-18.
The latest PLFS report is the first in the series of Annual report conducted
during the calendar year (January 2025-December 2025). As per the report, the
estimated Unemployment Rate (UR) on usual status for youth of age 15-29 years
has decreased from 10.3% in 2024 to 9.9% in 2025 in the country. State/UT-wise
and year-wise information is available in the PLFS reports which may be seen at
the website of MoSPI at https://www.mospi.gov.in/publications-reports.
The KLEMS database published by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides
employment estimates, including manufacturing sector, at all India level. As per
the latest data of the database, employment in the country increased to 64.33
crore in 2023-24 as compared to 47.5 crore in 2017-18. Total increase in
employment during 2017-18 to 2023-24 is about 16.83 crore (provisional) which
translate into 2.8 crore employment per year.

CSR FUNDS IN NASHIK
186. SHRI RAJABHAU PARAG PRAKASH WAJE:
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the total amount of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds generated by
companies operating in Nashik district during the last five financial years,
company-wise, year-wise and sector-wise;
(b) the details of CSR amount actually spent within Nashik district on local
priorities such as education, healthcare, drinking water, skill development and
rural infrastructure and the amount that was diverted outside the district;
(c) whether the Government is aware that despite being a major industrial and
agri-export hub, Nashik continues to face poor school infrastructure,
healthcare gaps and farmer distress, if so, the details thereof; and
(d) whether the Government proposes to mandate or incentivize local CSR
spending in the districts where companies generate profits, to ensure fair
regional development, if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS;
AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS (SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA):
(a) to (d): The legal framework for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is
provided through Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘the Act’), Schedule
VII of the Act and Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014. Under the Companies

Act, CSR is a Board driven process and the Board of the company is empowered
to plan, decide, execute and monitor CSR activities of the company based on the
recommendation of its CSR Committee. This Committee formulates and
recommends the CSR policy, which outlines the activities to be undertaken by the
company in alignment with the areas or subjects specified in Schedule VII of the
Act. The first proviso to Section 135 (5) of the Act provides that the company shall
give preference to the local area and areas around it where it operates. However,
the emphasis on local area is only directory and not mandatory in nature and
companies need to balance local area preference with national priorities. The
Government does not issue any specific direction to the companies to spend in
any particular geographical area or for any particular activity.
All data related to CSR filed by companies in MCA21 registry including
State-wise, District-wise, year-wise, Development Sector-wise, project-wise and
company–wise, are available in public domain and can be accessed at
www.csr.gov.in. On the basis of annual filings made by companies in the MCA 21
registry, the Sector-wise details of CSR expenditure in Nashik for the last five
Financial Years (FY) i.e. FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25 is given in the enclosed
Statement.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION; AND
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH
EASTERN REGION (DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR):
(a) to (d): Education is in the concurrent list and both the Central Government and
State Governments work together for its improvement. The Government of India
has launched the PM-Vidyalaxmi, a new central sector scheme in November
2024. Any student, who gets merit-based admission in top Quality Higher
Education Institutions (QHEIs) and who desires to avail the education loan can
get collateral-free and guarantor-free education loan under the scheme. There is
no upper limit on number of students getting such loans. Since the launch of this
scheme on 6th November, 2024 till 12th July, 2026, 108106 PM Vidyalaxmi

All the top 100 ranked HEIs in the overall/ category-specific and/or domain
specific rankings in the list of National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) list;
plus all the top 200 ranked HEIs under the governance of State/UT governments
in the list of NIRF; plus all remaining HEIs under the governance of Government
of India are included in the list of QHEIs. A total of 1051 QHEIs, including 138
QHEIs from the state of Tamil Nadu have been included under the PM Vidyalaxmi
Scheme.
Further, for students with annual family income up to ₹8 lakh, the scheme
provides 3% interest subvention on loans up to ₹10 lakh. Each year up to one
lakh fresh students not getting any other scholarship or interest subvention on
education loan will get this interest subvention benefit. An outlay of ₹ 3,600 crore
has been made from 2024-25 to 2030-31, for providing 3% interest subvention
benefit for up to 7 lakh fresh students during this period.
The State-wise and year-wise number of PM-Vidyalaxmi education loans
and amount sanctioned along with Institute-wise number of students from the
state of Tamil Nadu who have benefitted under the scheme since its launch is
given in the enclosed Statement.

Rs. 60,000 crore (Central Share – Rs. 30,000 crore, State Share – Rs. 20,000
crore and Industry Share – Rs. 10,000 crore).
The scheme comprises of two components:
i. Component I – Upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and
800 Spoke ITIs) in a Hub and Spoke model wherein upgradation includes
smart classrooms, modern labs, digital content, and new courses aligned to
industry needs.
ii. Component II – Capacity Augmentation of five NSTIs located in
Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur, and Ludhiana, including
setting-up sector-specific National Centres of Excellence for skilling, with
focus on advanced training of trainers with global partnership, and
curriculum development.
The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transfromation through
Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) Scheme is being implemented across States/UTs,
including Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, to upgrade the quality and
relevance of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). The National Steering
Committee (NSC) has approved six (6) Strategic Investment Plans (SIPs)
submitted by Anchor Industry Partners (AIPs), comprising three from Telangana,
one from Andhra Pradesh, one from Odisha and one from Gujarat. The details of
the approved clusters, along with the names of the Anchor Industry Partners, are
provided in Table 1 below.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF MICRO, SMALL AND
MEDIUM ENTERPRISES; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT (KUMARI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE):
(a) to (e): The Government of India has implemented four Labour Codes, namely,
the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on
Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working
Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020 with effect from 21st November, 2025. The
Central Rules under the said Labour Codes have been notified on 8th May, 2026.
Since ‘Labour’ falls under the concurrent subject, the States/UTs are also
required to frame Rules under the Labour Codes. The Ministry of Labour and
Employment is proactively engaged with the States/UTs for finalisation of their
rules and smooth implementation of the Codes. Accordingly, most of the
States/UTs have already taken measures & have finalised or published/pre-
published the Rules under the Labour Codes and a few States/UTs are in the
process of pre-publishing/finalising the Rules.
The four Labour Codes were passed after extensive consultations with all
stakeholders including States/UTs. The comments/concerns raised by the

the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on
Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working
Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020 with effect from 21st November, 2025. The
Central Rules under the said Labour Codes have been notified on 8th May, 2026.
Since ‘Labour’ falls under the concurrent subject, the States/UTs are also
required to frame Rules under the Labour Codes. The Ministry of Labour and
Employment is proactively engaged with the States/UTs for finalisation of their
rules and smooth implementation of the Codes. Accordingly, most of the
States/UTs have already taken measures & have finalised or published/pre-
published the Rules under the Labour Codes and a few States/UTs are in the
process of pre-publishing/finalising the Rules.

stakeholders including States/UTs. The comments/concerns raised by the

TOURISM DEVELOPMENT IN BIHAR
205. SHRI RAJA RAM SINGH:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has undertaken an assessment of tourism
infrastructure gaps across major heritage and religious destinations in
Bihar, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the details of the funds released and utilised under Central tourism
schemes in Bihar during the last five years; and
(c) whether the Government is considering any major programme to develop
tourism in Rohtas district of Bihar and if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI
GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT):
(a): Development of tourism infrastructure, amenities and experiences at
tourist destinations is primarily undertaken by the concerned State
Government and Union Territory Administration. However, the Ministry of
Tourism, under its various schemes such as Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and
Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD), Swadesh Darshan (SD),
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge Based Destination Development
(CBDD) provides financial assistance for the development of tourism
infrastructure across the country including Bihar.
(b): The details of the funds released and utilized for the projects under the
said schemes in Bihar are given in the enclosed Statement.

(d): Under Samagra Shiksha, there is a dedicated Inclusive Education
component for various interventions such as Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya
(KGBVs) residential schools from class VI to XII, for girls belonging to
disadvantaged groups such as SC, ST, OBC, Minority and Below Poverty Line
(BPL), Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Avasiya Vidyalayas which provide
residential facilities for both girls and boys belonging to Socio Economically
Disadvantaged Groups (SEDGs). Further, the educational needs of children
from the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) are addressed through
the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) and
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) Schemes, provision of
transport allowance and undertaking enrolment & retention drives.
Special training for age-appropriate admission of out of school children
and residential as well as non-residential training for older children, seasonal
hostels / residential camps, special training centres at worksites, transport/
escort facility etc. are also supported to bring out of school children to the
formal schooling system.
Under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE)
Act, 2009, provision for free textbooks and uniforms are provided to children
from SEDGs. Further, Section 12 of RTE Act, 2009 provides for 25% seats to
be provided to EWS category of students in private-unaided schools. Further,

PROTECTION AND PRESERVATION OF WETLANDS IN ASSAM
208. SHRI KAMAKHYA PRASAD TASA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of all the existing wetlands across the country, State/UT-wise,
particularly in Assam;
(b) the details of such wetlands that need protection and preservation,
State/UT-wise, particularly in Assam;
(c) whether any steps have been taken towards the protection and
preservation of such wetlands;
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reason therefor; and
(e) whether the Government has any plan for the wetlands to be converted
into ecotourism, while allowing controlled recreational activities like
birdwatching and nature photography etc. and if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST
AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH):

(a) whether Government envisages to start one Navodaya Vidyalaya (NV) in
each district of the country, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether it is true that only 13 districts out of 28 have NVs in Andhra
Pradesh and if so, the details thereof;

districts?
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT
AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF EDUCATION (SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY):
(a) to (e): The Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme envisages for opening of one
Navodaya Vidyalaya (NV) in each district of the country. Opening of new NVs
is a continuous process which depends on the willingness of the concerned
State Government/UT administration to make available requisite suitable land,
free of cost, for construction of the permanent building and making available
required temporary building, free of rent, to run the Vidyalaya till the permanent
building is constructed. Sanction and opening of new NVs depends on
approval by the competent authority as per extant procedures. As on date, a
total of 694 NVs have been sanctioned across the country, including 28
additional NVs.
At present, 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh have been covered under
Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme. Further, two additional NVs, which were
sanctioned in Prakasam (now Markapuram) and East Godavari (now
Polavaram) on basis of SC/ST concentrated areas, are also functional. Thus,
total 15 NVs are functional in the State. List of NVs in the State of Andhra
Pradesh is given in the enclosed Statement.

udgement_29-May-2026.pdf

should endeavour to conduct the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) periodically,

Education, Government of India with the objective to create a multi-layered
inter-disciplinary and inter-sectorial efficient professional technical manpower.
To align with New Education Policy (NEP) 2020, higher educational
institutions are expected to evolve into multidisciplinary institutions.

issue of Letter of Intent. Accordingly, the Ministry of Education issued Letter of
Intent (LoI) on 08.12.2025 to the Ghani Khan Choudhury Institute of

concentration in the relevant market. The Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (“HHI”)

specific facts and market conditions of each case.

concerns relating to barriers to entry arising from high spectrum costs and

digital markets, data leverage, privacy, and vertical integration require case-
by-case assessment under the Competition Act, 2002. The study does not
record any specific finding of collusive conduct and notes that existing vertical
integration was generally viewed by stakeholders as pro-competitive and not
posing any imminent competition concern.

sector. CCI has also passed final orders in 6 cases each relating to the
telecom and cement sectors during this period.

Maharashtra is pending for consideration or approval before the National
Steering Committee (NSC).

Maharashtra amounting to ₹50 lakh for engagement of a Project Management
Consultant (PMC) and ₹30 lakh for Industry Outreach activities during FY

(b) the details of the key sectors identified under the cultural and creative

governance, if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;

THE MINISTER OF CULTURE; AND MINISTER OF TOURISM (SHRI

(a): The Ministry of Culture has formulated a Cultural and Creative Economy
intervention, namely Rachnatmak Bharat, for the promotion and development of

pages.original_text:

the cultural and creative economy. The proposed strategy envisages
interventions for capacity building, market access, innovation, digital enablement
and institutional strengthening with a view to promoting sustainable growth of
the creative economy, including support for emerging artists and creative
practitioners.
(b): The proposed intervention broadly covers sectors such as visual arts,
performing arts, museums, cultural heritage, architecture, digital creative
industries and other creative services.
(c): The Ministry regularly engages with stakeholders, experts, cultural
institutions and other Ministries/Departments, as and when required, for policy
formulation and implementation of its programmes.
(d): The Ministry promotes cultural activities through preservation and promotion
of cultural heritage, support to artists and cultural institutions, organization of
cultural events, and international cultural exchanges, which contribute to
employment and livelihood opportunities in the cultural sector.
(e): The initiatives of the Ministry contribute to the promotion of India's cultural
heritage, tourism, cultural exchanges and livelihood opportunities across the
country, including the State of Maharashtra. No State-specific assessment of the
contribution of the cultural and creative sector to economic growth or cultural
diplomacy is maintained by the Ministry.

An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 was
conducted by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management
(AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of Ministry of Finance, Government of
India. As per the report, PMKVY training has contributed to a measurable shift
in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. The
combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased
from 26.6% prior to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting an 18.8
percentage point increase. Income- related outcomes also show positive
movement, with 41.4% of STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior
Learning (RPL) candidates reporting an increase in income following training
and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded access to
formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable
improvements in skill confidence, employment participation, and income
outcomes for a substantial proportion of beneficiaries.

industry requirements.

States and grower institutions. The study should establish disease-stage-

specific protocols; per-hectare input, labour and diagnostic costs; maintenance
period; drainage and replantation needs; and beneficiary verification
safeguards. Based on this study, the Ministry should revise relevant MIDH
norms and create a disease-specific component for plantation gardens, with

in the public domain.

(xv) Need to ensure direct procurement of paddy by FCI and prompt
payment to farmers in Kerala
SHRI KODIKUNNIL SURESH (MAVELIKKARA): I wish to draw the attention
of the Government to the difficulties faced by paddy farmers in Kerala,
particularly in Kuttanad, one of the country's most important rice-producing
regions, under the existing Paddy Receipt Sheet (PRS)-based payment
mechanism. Under the Decentralised Procurement (DCP) Scheme, farmers
receive payment through bank loans against PRS instead of direct payment for
the paddy procured. Although the State Government guarantees repayment,
farmers are treated as borrowers, adversely affecting their CIBIL scores and
limiting their access to institutional credit. I urge the Government to consider
enabling the Food Corporation of India (FCI) to procure paddy directly from
farmers in Kerala, especially in Kuttanad, and ensure direct payment within 3–
7 days. Alternatively, the PRS mechanism should be delinked from the
individual farmer's CIBIL records so that farmers are not shown as bank
borrowers for Government-guaranteed procurement payments. Such

any violation. The renewal process lacks transparency, with organisations
often denied clear reasons or a fair opportunity to respond. Undefined terms
such as *"proselytization"* create legal uncertainty and risk arbitrary
enforcement. Further, broad definitions and harsh compliance requirements

not attract cancellation of registration or confiscation of assets. Permanent
seizure of assets must be limited to proven cases involving national security or
deliberate fraud, and only after due adjudication and exhaustion of statutory
appeals. Since 2012, only about 14,455 of 52,159 FCRA-registered
organisations remain active, highlighting the far-reaching impact of such
decisions. I urge the Government to reconsider these provisions after wider
stakeholder consultation.

(xxi) Need for establishment of a Kendriya Vidyalaya in Mathurapur
Parliamentary Constituency, West Bengal
SHRI BAPI HALDAR (MATHURAPUR): I wish to draw the attention of the
Government to the urgent need for establishing a Kendriya Vidyalaya in the
Mathurapur Parliamentary Constituency of West Bengal. Mathurapur, which
includes a large part of the Sundarbans region, is one of the relatively
underdeveloped and geographically challenging areas of the country. Owing to
its remote location, fragile ecology and limited educational infrastructure,
students have comparatively fewer opportunities to access quality school
education. Despite this, there is no Kendriya Vidyalaya in the constituency. As
a result, children of Central Government employees, Defence and Paramilitary
personnel, Railway, Postal and other transferable employees, as well as
deserving local students, are compelled to travel long distances or seek
admission outside the Constituency, causing considerable hardship.
Establishment of a Kendriya Vidyalaya in Mathurapur would significantly
strengthen educational infrastructure in this aspirational region, ensure access
to quality education, and provide equal educational opportunities to students
living in the remote Sundarbans area. I, therefore, urge the Government to
accord priority to the establishment of a Kendriya Vidyalaya in the Mathurapur
Parliamentary Constituency at the earliest after completing the necessary
feasibility assessment and procedural formalities.

(xxii) Regarding likely adverse impact on Tamil Nadu due to proposed
construction of Mekedatu Balancing Reservoir on River Cauvery
by Karnataka
DR. KALANIDHI VEERASWAMY (CHENNAI NORTH): I would like to draw
the attention of the Government towards a matter of urgent public importance
regarding the proposed construction of the Mekedatu Balancing Reservoir
Project by the Government of Karnataka across the River Cauvery. The
proposed project has caused widespread concern in Tamil Nadu, as it has the
potential to adversely affect the assured flow of Cauvery waters to the lower
riparian state. Tamil Nadu's farmers, particularly those in the Cauvery Delta
region, are critically dependent on the timely release of Cauvery waters for
irrigation, drinking water needs, and sustaining agricultural livelihoods. The
Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal, in its final award, and the judgment of the
Hon'ble Supreme Court have determined the allocation of Cauvery waters
among the basin States. The Cauvery basin has been recognized as a water-
deficit basin, and any new storage project undertaken without the concurrence
of the co-basin states and without the approval of the competent statutory
authorities would raise serious concerns regarding the implementation of the
existing legal framework governing inter-state river water sharing. The
Government of Tamil Nadu and the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly have
consistently opposed the Mekedatu project, maintaining that it could prejudice
the legitimate and legally protected water rights of the lower riparian state and
adversely impact millions of farmers and citizens dependent on the Cauvery

(xxiii) Need to address the problems being faced by employees of BSNL
in the country
SHRI BASTIPATI NAGARAJU (KURNOOL): I would like to highlight the
urgent crisis facing the employees of BSNL. This public sector organisation is
the backbone of India’s telecom network, connecting our most remote and
rural areas. During national emergencies, natural disasters, and the COVID-19
pandemic, BSNL workers served with absolute dedication. Tragically, over 380
of these workers lost their lives while keeping our nation connected. Yet, their
immense sacrifices remain completely unrewarded. Today, these employees'
rightful salary hike under the 3rd Pay Revision Commission has been delayed
for years. Retirees are waiting indefinitely for their pensions to be updated. Pay
and promotions between different categories of staff and their medical benefits
have been deeply cut. Therefore, I request the hon’ble Government to grant
an immediate waiver of the affordability clause for the implementation of 3rd
PRC and finalise wage negotiation for non-executives; delink pension revision
